conventions.convention: The bounded-domain residual estimate assumes AC_ω, a bounded connected C1 Euclidean domain, continuously extending interior derivatives, zero boundary velocity, and an explicitly assumed zero-trace Poincare constant.

The periodic channel is represented by periodic lifts in x,z and Lebesgue integration over one fundamental cell. Its Poincare bound has the valid, nonsharp constant h; the cell is not treated as a bounded C1 Euclidean domain.
Couette perturbation energy is E(t)=∫Q|u−(Sy,0,0)|², without a factor of one half or density. The decay estimate concerns an already-existing smooth solution on [0,T] and requires |S|h²/ν<2.

The vortex-sheet model has equal positive densities, no gravity or surface tension, upper and lower decaying harmonic potentials, kinematic equations (∂t+U±∂x)η=∂yφ±, and continuous pressure perturbations p′±=−ρ0(∂t+U±∂x)φ±.
Normal modes use exp(ikx+λt) with k>0. Periodic Fourier coefficients use normalization 1/(2π), and the squared Hm norm is Σj(1+j²)^m|η̂j|².

load_bearing.statement: Assuming AC_ω, on a bounded C1 domain, smooth divergence-free zero-trace fields satisfying −μΔw+∇q=f and the stated Poincare inequality obey ||∇w||₂≤CΩ||f||₂/μ and ||w||₂≤CΩ²||f||₂/μ. Separately, C1 periodic-channel fields vanishing at both walls satisfy ||v||₂≤h||∇v||₂.
Assuming AC_ω and the stated smooth incompressible Navier-Stokes solution, periodic channel and Couette wall data, if |S|h²/ν<2 then E(t)≤exp[−(2ν/h²−|S|)t]E(0) for every t∈[0,T].

For the stated equal-density harmonic linear interface model, a nonzero-amplitude mode with k>0 requires λ=−ik(U++U−)/2±k|U+−U−|/2. A nonzero velocity jump gives a real growing solution, and for every fixed t>0 the constructed periodic mode sequence has bounded initial Hm norm and unbounded evolved Hm norm.
